title: OneShop Pricing 2026: Is $45/Month Worth It?
summary: OneShop only has one simplified plan for $45 a month. See what's included, who it's worth it for, and how Vendoo compares for part-time resellers.
body_markdown:
OneShop pricing is $45 a month for a single plan, and every seller pays the same amount whether they list 15 items or 1,000


. That plan gets you crosslisting to Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, and Depop, plus auto-delisting and Poshmark automation, with a 7-day free trial before the first charge. It can be a good fit for some high volume sellers, but for part-time resellers or anyone who wants to sell on more than four marketplaces, it's worth looking at other options before making your choice.


## Main Takeaways


- OneShop costs $45 a month for a single plan with no cheaper options.


- A seller listing 15 items a month pays $3 per item in software costs, while someone listing 1,500 pays 3 cents. The flat rate pricing works best for high-volume sellers.


- If Poshmark is your main platform, OneShop's automation for sharing and sending offers can save you a lot of time.


- OneShop only lists to Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, and Depop. If your inventory sells better on other marketplaces like Etsy, Grailed, or Facebook Marketplace, you'll need a different tool.


- OneShop only works in the US and Canada, so sellers in the UK, Australia, and other countries will need another option.


- Vendoo, another option with similar features, starts at $12.49 a month billed annually and includes unlimited items and 10+ marketplaces, so you can start small and upgrade when your business is ready.


## The OneShop Flat-Rate Model Explained


OneShop got rid of their original four plan model and


simplified things with a single subscription option. Here’s what it gets you:


- **The $45 Monthly Fee:** For $45 a month you get the OneShop app on iOS and Android, crosslisting, auto-delisting, and the Poshmark automation which includes sharing, following, and sending offers to likers. There are no add-ons to buy, which keeps things simple, and you get a 7-day free trial before the first charge.


- **The "All or Nothing" Problem:** A seller listing 15 items a month pays exactly the same $45 as a seller listing 1,500 each month. Break that down and the part time seller pays $3 per item in software costs while the high volume seller pays 3 cents. This is great for sellers who list a lot, but if you're flipping on weekends and trying to keep overhead low, the cost can end up not being worth it.


- **Marketplace Limitations:** While the tool has important features like auto-delist, which keeps you from double selling, it only syncs across four platforms. If your inventory would do better on Etsy (vintage), Grailed (menswear), or Facebook Marketplace (furniture and bulky items), OneShop can't help you list there. You'd be listing on those platforms manually and remembering to delist them yourself when something sells.


## Geographic and Platform Restrictions


Beyond the price, there are a couple of other limits worth knowing about before you sign up.


- **US and Canada Only:** OneShop only supports US and Canadian marketplaces, so sellers in the UK, Australia, or other countries won't be able to use it. That leaves out a big part of the reselling community.


- **The Automation Focus:** OneShop's Poshmark automation is one of the features their users tend to like most. If Poshmark is your main platform, it can save you a lot of time on sharing and sending offers. The problem is, if Poshmark changes its algorithm or how it handles automated activity, your sales can take a big hit and there isn't much you can do about it. Expanding your reach by selling across 10+ marketplaces spreads that risk out.

## Finding Better ROI with Vendoo


If paying $45 a month and only getting access to four marketplaces doesn’t sound like the right fit for you, Vendoo is worth a look. Other competitors claim that


OneShop is still considered pretty pricey compared to other tools that do the same job. Vendoo gets you more marketplaces for less money, and the plans are set up so you're not paying for features you don't need yet.


### Plans That Scale With You:


Vendoo's Starter plan is $12.49 a month when billed annually, or $14.99 when you pay month to month. It includes unlimited items and access to every marketplace Vendoo supports.


That covers what most part-time sellers need: crosslisting, sale detection, importing, delist and relist, listing templates, and profit tracking. As your business picks up and you want things like AI listing help or bulk actions for managing a lot of listings, you can move up to the Growth plan at $24.99 a month billed annually.


Higher plans add features like automated offers and marketplace sharing, which is the closest match to what OneShop does on Poshmark. The difference is you only upgrade when your business can handle it, instead of starting at $45 on day one. You can see the full breakdown on[Vendoo's pricing page](https://www.vendoo.co/pricing) .


### 10+ Marketplace Reach:


When you draft an item in Vendoo, you can send it to the same four marketplaces OneShop covers, plus more than six more including Grailed, Facebook Marketplace, and Etsy. That's more than twice as many places for buyers to find your items. It also lets you list your inventory where it sells best.


### Instant Sale Detection:


When an item sells on eBay, Vendoo detects the sale and delists it from your other connected marketplaces automatically. That protects your seller metrics, since canceling an order because the item already sold somewhere else can count against you on platforms like eBay.


Sale detection currently works with Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, Depop, and Whatnot. If something sells on another platform, you can delist it everywhere else from directly inside Vendoo.


### True Cloud & Mobile Freedom:


Vendoo has native iOS and Android apps, so you're not stuck working on a computer if that doesn’t fit your workflow. You can literally take photos, edit them, create the listing, and crosslist it while you're still at the thrift store.


For part-time sellers who often like to list in little pockets of time, that makes it a lot easier to get a few items up whenever you have ten minutes.


## Conclusion


OneShop pricing makes the most sense for high-volume sellers in the US or Canada who mostly sell on Poshmark and want automation. For part-time sellers, or anyone who wants to reach buyers on Etsy, Grailed, or Facebook Marketplace, paying $45 per month for the tool is harder to justify. By comparison, Vendoo starts at a lower price, supports more marketplaces, and lets you upgrade as your business grows, so you're only paying for what you actually need.


## FAQs


### **How much does OneShop cost in 2026?**


OneShop costs $45 a month for all sellers. There are no cheaper tiers or add-ons, so every seller pays the same price no matter how many items they list. That covers crosslisting to Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, and Depop, plus auto-delisting, the mobile app, and Poshmark automation. There is a 7 day free trial before you have to pay.


### **Does OneShop have a free trial?**


Yes, OneShop offers a 7-day free trial before you have to start paying $45 per month.


### **Can I use OneShop outside the US?**


Other than the US, Canada is the only other country OneShop supports. Sellers in the UK, Australia, and other countries won't be able to use it for their local marketplaces, so they'll need a different crosslisting tool.


### **Which marketplaces does OneShop support?**


OneShop crosslists to four marketplaces: Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, and Depop.


### **Is Vendoo cheaper than OneShop?**


Yes, Vendoo has cheaper plans than OneShop, which can be a great advantage to smaller scale resellers. Vendoo's Starter plan is $12.49 a month billed annually, or $14.99 month to month, compared to OneShop's $45. Starter includes unlimited items, all 10+ marketplaces, sale detection, and the mobile app.
